---
title: "Before the course"
---
Before the course you read the case study and the paper and create the account that the raw files need, which takes about two to three hours. Nothing has to be installed beforehand, because day 1 ends with the tools installed and the data downloaded, with time to solve the problems that installations raise. Installing R, Quarto and an IDE (Positron, RStudio, VS Code, etc.) before day 1 is optional.

## 1. The case study

[Read the case study](../../cases/eu-frames/index.qmd){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

The case study presents the original study and its data, SCORE and the Multi100 project, the five reanalyses and the replications. Every part of the course works on this case.

## 2. The paper

[Open the paper](https://doi.org/10.1093/esr/jcw008){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

Read the paper of the original author (OA), which day 1 discusses in full: its question, its data, its measures and its models. The reference is also on the case study.

## 3. The account at GESIS

[Open the GESIS archive](https://search.gesis.org){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

Create a free account at the GESIS archive, which the download of the Eurobarometer files on day 1 needs.

## 4. R, Quarto and an IDE (optional)

[Install R and the workspace](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"}

If you would rather install R, Quarto and an IDE before day 1, follow the steps for your operating system on the setup page of the AR4DS site.

**By the start of the course** you know what the claim is and how the paper supports it, and you have the account with which you will download the raw files on day 1.
